title: Paul Gonsalves falling off his chair in Las Vegas and on Italian television
summary: Two stories of Paul Gonsalves tumbling on stage, including Duke's quip that he did not drink and the Italian TV show with Ella.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: How about (Inaudible) Paul Gonsalves?
Oh, I think he was possibly one of the most

beautiful human beings I ever met, you know, as a person. And -- but I remember one time I was in Vegas with Nancy Wilson, and Duke was in the Sahara. We were working at the -- oh, I can't think of the name of the hotel. The Sands. So we went down to catch Duke's band after we finished our show, and Paul fell down, and Paul was sober as a judge, you know, he fell, he was on the stand.
Was this after he had arthritis, or was this --
No, he was just. He just --
How did he fall down?
Off of his chair.
Sleeping?

No, he just happened to fall down. But the way he stood up. He stood up and held his horn up to let everybody know that he was all right. And Duke walked to the mike and said, 'Isn't that amazing? This man doesn't even drink.'
(Laughter)
And we broke up.
(Laughter)
Another time -- I hope I'm not --
You haven't talked about (Inaudible).
No. Well, there was a time when we were in Italy, and this was with Ella, Ella Fitzgerald and Duke Ellington. So I'm conducting the band from the piano, and I

could see Paul to my left. He was -- well, he was feeling pretty good that night. And they had a big television show going on. They were televising this thing. And in the middle of our set we would always get -- we would use the trio and put some ballads in and go back and use -- go back to the band, you know?
Uh-huh.

And I could see this leg coming up off of the chair. This is Paul's chair. But I'm watching Ella out in front, you know, because I've got to watch her. And I saw Paul begin to lean over and lean over, and he was going.
(Laughter)
And he fell on the floor, and you know what he did when he got up? He looked out to the audience and said, 'Ssh, don't tell nobody.'
(Laughter)
And the television cameras were all over the stage and Ella Fitzgerald had to stop singing, because it was -- the audience broke up laughing. He said, 'Ssh, don't tell anybody.'
(Laughter)

And then, on the intermission between shows, he says, 'Man, did you see me when I dropped my horn?' I said, 'You fell on the floor, man. You did much more than dropping your horn.' He thought he just dropped his horn.
